dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Anita. How can I help you?

Good morning, Anita. My name is Isabel Souza. I rent a little place, and the landlord says it's fine with him, I want to add a deck off the back. Does that need a permit? And an inspection, I suppose?
Good morning, Ms. Souza. A deck generally does need a permit, and yes, there's usually an inspection too. Can I ask a couple of things? Is it attached to the house, or free-standing?

Attached. Off the back door. There's just a step now, a concrete one. My husband's family had a porch like that in the old days, with the whole family out there every Sunday, oh, the noise. Anyway. I'm sorry, I wander. Attached, yes.
That's all right. And roughly how high off the ground would it be, do you know? Just a couple steps up, or higher?
Two steps, I'd say. Maybe three. I'd have to look.
Okay. Even at that height, attached to the house, you'd want to apply for a deck permit. The inspector would look at the footings and the framing before it's covered, and then a final once it's done.
I see. Now, does a licensed contractor have to be the one to apply? Or can I do it myself? Well, the landlord, I mean. I'm only renting.

Good question. The property owner can usually apply for their own permit, or a licensed contractor can apply on the owner's behalf. As a tenant, you'd need the owner involved, either signing the application or giving written permission. I'd have him call us or come in.

Oh, he'll do that. He's a good man. Could you call me back if there's more paperwork? Though, I should tell you, my voicemail is full. I haven't figured out how to clear it. My niece set it up and I never learned.

Sure, I can note your number, but if the voicemail's full we couldn't leave a message. Better that your landlord reaches out, or you call back here during the day. We're open weekdays. Would you like the number for this office repeated?
No, I have it right here on the refrigerator. I'll call back. Is that everything, then? Permit, inspection, the owner signs?
That's it. Deck permit, inspections along the way, and the owner applies or authorizes a licensed contractor to. When he's ready, he can bring a simple sketch with the size of the deck.
A sketch. I can do that. Thank you, Anita. That's very clear.
You're welcome, Ms. Souza. Have a good day.
